primary_acts: Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021
metadata.description: Complete structured explainable dataset for core Indian cyber laws with prevention and legal mapping intelligence.
metadata.disclaimer: For legal awareness only. Not a substitute for professional legal advice.

laws_master.section_title: Penalty for Unauthorized Access & Damage to Computer System
laws_master.full_description: If any person without permission of the owner or person in charge of a computer, accesses, downloads, introduces virus, disrupts, denies access, or damages any computer system, he shall be liable to pay damages.

punishment.details: Liable to pay damages by way of compensation not exceeding ₹1 crore to the affected person.

preventive_measures: Install firewall and endpoint protection
Enable intrusion detection/prevention systems
Restrict administrative privileges
Implement principle of least privilege
Perform regular security audits and VAPT
Maintain access logs and monitor them

laws_master.section_title: Compensation for Failure to Protect Data
laws_master.full_description: Body corporate possessing, dealing or handling sensitive personal data is liable to compensate affected persons for negligence in implementing reasonable security practices causing wrongful loss or wrongful gain.
legal_ingredients: Body corporate handling sensitive personal data
Wrongful loss or wrongful gain to any person

punishment.details: Liable to pay damages by way of compensation to the affected person.

preventive_measures: Implement ISO 27001 or equivalent security standards
Conduct regular security audits
Appoint a data protection officer
Create a data breach response plan
Provide employee training on data handling
Encrypt sensitive personal data

laws_master.full_description: Whoever knowingly or intentionally conceals, destroys or alters any computer source code used for computer, computer programme, computer system or computer network when source code is required to be kept or maintained by law.
legal_ingredients: Source code is required to be kept or maintained by law
preventive_measures: Implement version control systems (e.g., Git)
Restrict source code access based on roles
Maintain secure, encrypted backups of source code
Use code repositories with detailed access logs
Conduct regular code audits
Execute employee confidentiality agreements
evidence_required: Original and altered source code versions

laws_master.full_description: If any person dishonestly or fraudulently does any act referred to in Section 43, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term up to three years or with fine up to ₹5,00,000 or with both. [citation:4]
legal_ingredients: Commission of acts under Section 43 (unauthorized access, data download, etc.)
preventive_measures: Implement strong access controls (MFA)
Deploy intrusion detection and prevention systems
Apply regular security patches and updates
Conduct employee background verification
Use activity monitoring software
Provide security awareness training
evidence_required: Evidence of fraud or dishonest conduct

laws_master.full_description: Whoever dishonestly receives or retains any stolen computer resource or communication device knowing or having reason to believe the same to be stolen computer resource or communication device. [citation:4]
legal_ingredients: Stolen computer resource or communication device
Knowledge or reason to believe it is stolen
preventive_measures: Verify device provenance and IMEI before purchase
Check IMEI/Serial numbers against stolen databases (CEIR)
Maintain original purchase receipts and invoices
Register devices with manufacturer
Use device tracking software
Report stolen devices immediately to police and portal

laws_master.full_description: Fraudulent or dishonest use of electronic signature, password, OTP or any other unique identification feature of another person. [citation:1][citation:4]
legal_ingredients: Use of another person's digital identity feature
preventive_measures: Enable two-factor or multi-factor authentication
Never share OTP, passwords, or CVV
Secure SIM card with a PIN lock
Monitor login alerts and account activity
Use strong, unique passwords for each account
evidence_required: Bank account statements showing fraudulent transactions
IP address details of the perpetrator

laws_master.section_title: Cheating by Personation Using Computer Resource
laws_master.full_description: Cheating someone by pretending to be another person using any computer resource or communication device. [citation:1][citation:4]
legal_ingredients: Dishonest inducement to deliver property or consent
Use of computer resource or communication device
preventive_measures: Avoid scanning unknown QR codes for payments
Verify payment requests through independent channels
Cross-check official contact numbers from verified sources
Be wary of urgent requests for money/favors
Do not share personal details on unsolicited calls
evidence_required: UPI ID or bank account details of scammer

laws_master.full_description: Capturing, publishing or transmitting private images of any person in mass or personal space without their consent. [citation:1]
legal_ingredients: Private area of a person captured
preventive_measures: Do not share intimate content with anyone
Use secure cloud storage with strong passwords
Be cautious of apps requesting camera/gallery permissions
Disable camera access for suspicious apps
Regularly review app permissions on devices
evidence_required: Screenshots of the content being shared
Metadata logs (time, date, location) of the image
URLs where the image was published
Device IMEI from where it was captured/uploaded

laws_master.full_description: Acts using computer resources that threaten the sovereignty, unity and integrity, or security of India, or to strike terror in the people. [citation:4]
legal_ingredients: Intent to threaten national security or strike terror
Use of computer systems to cause harm
Denial of access to critical information systems
preventive_measures: Monitor critical information infrastructure
Implement air-gapping for sensitive systems
Conduct regular security drills and audits
Report any suspicious cyber threats to CERT-In/law enforcement
Employ stringent access controls for protected systems
evidence_required: System attack logs and network traffic data
Evidence linking the act to national security threat

laws_master.section_title: Publishing Obscene Material in Electronic Form
laws_master.full_description: Whoever publishes or transmits or causes to be published in electronic form any material which is lascivious or appeals to prurient interest or tends to deprave and corrupt persons. [citation:1]
legal_ingredients: Tends to deprave and corrupt persons
preventive_measures: Implement robust content moderation policies
Use AI-based content filtering tools
Establish clear terms of service prohibiting obscene content
Provide easy user reporting mechanisms
Conduct regular platform audits
evidence_required: Uploader's IP address and account information
Server logs showing the content hosted

laws_master.full_description: Whoever publishes or transmits or causes to be published any material containing sexually explicit act or conduct in electronic form. [citation:1]
legal_ingredients: Material contains sexually explicit act or conduct
Absence of lawful exception or defense
preventive_measures: Strict content moderation with human review
Implement robust age verification systems
Utilize photo-DNA/hashing to block known illegal content
Provide clear 'report abuse' mechanisms
Maintain immediate takedown procedures
evidence_required: Detailed screenshots or video recordings of content

laws_master.full_description: Publishing, browsing, downloading or transmitting material depicting children in sexually explicit act in electronic form. [citation:1]
legal_ingredients: Material depicts children in sexually explicit act
preventive_measures: Do not forward, save, or share such content under any circumstance
Immediately report to law enforcement and platforms
Use parental control software to protect children
Educate children on online safety and risks
Implement and use photo-DNA/hashing to detect illegal content

laws_master.section_title: Preservation and Retention of Information by Intermediaries
laws_master.full_description: Intermediaries shall preserve and retain such information as may be prescribed for such duration and in such manner and format as the Central Government may prescribe. [citation:4]
legal_ingredients: Information was required to be preserved by rules
preventive_measures: Comply with CERT-In directions for log retention (180 days)
Maintain secure, immutable storage for logs
Implement centralized log collection and monitoring (SIEM)
Establish a clear data retention and disposal policy
Ensure logs are time-synchronized (NTP)
evidence_required: Evidence of log storage location and duration
Access logs to the log repository
Proof of compliance with CERT-In directions

laws_master.section_title: Powers to Issue Directions for Interception/Monitoring
laws_master.full_description: Central/State Government may issue directions to intercept, monitor or decrypt any information through computer resource in the interest of sovereignty, security, public order or for investigation of any offence.
preventive_measures: Maintain proper records of all government directions
Designate a nodal compliance officer
Implement technical capabilities for lawful interception (within law)
Ensure secure and confidential handling of requests
Provide regular compliance training to staff

laws_master.section_title: Power to Issue Directions for Blocking Public Access
laws_master.full_description: Central Government may issue directions to block public access to any information through any computer resource in the interest of sovereignty, security, public order or to prevent incitement to an offence. [citation:1]
preventive_measures: Establish a clear procedure for responding to government blocking orders
Implement technical ability to block specific URLs/content
Maintain a confidential record of actions taken
Designate a point of contact for government agencies
evidence_required: Blocking order from authorized government body
Records of compliance (e.g., date and time of blocking)
List of URLs/information that was blocked

laws_master.full_description: Whoever secures access or attempts to secure access to a protected system notified by the Central Government shall be punished. [citation:4]
legal_ingredients: Unauthorized access or attempt to access
preventive_measures: Implement multi-layer security architecture
Enforce strict access controls with biometric/MFA
Provide 24/7 security monitoring through a SOC
Conduct regular penetration testing and security audits
Maintain air-gapped systems where appropriate

laws_master.full_description: CERT-In serves as the national agency for cyber incident response. Mandatory reporting of cybersecurity incidents within 6 hours of noticing. [citation:1]
preventive_measures: Designate a 24x7 incident reporting coordinator
Maintain an incident response Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
Retain all ICT system logs for 180 days within India
Synchronize all system clocks with NTP servers (NIC/NPL)
Develop an incident classification matrix for quick reporting
evidence_required: Timestamp of when the incident was first detected
Copy of the initial notification sent to CERT-In

laws_master.full_description: Disclosure of any electronic record, book, register, information or material without consent in pursuance of any powers conferred under the IT Act.
legal_ingredients: Access to information under powers conferred by IT Act
Disclosure of such information without consent
preventive_measures: Have employees sign strict confidentiality agreements
Apply 'need-to-know' principle for data access
Establish clear data classification policies
Provide regular training on non-disclosure obligations
Maintain audit trails for all data access
Enforce penalties for unauthorized disclosure
evidence_required: Records showing who accessed the data
Proof of disclosure (e.g., copy of leaked information)
Consent records (or proof of absence of consent)

laws_master.section_title: Disclosure of Personal Information in Breach of Contract
laws_master.full_description: Disclosure of personal information about another person without consent in breach of a lawful contract with knowledge that disclosure will cause wrongful loss or gain. [citation:4]
legal_ingredients: Knowledge that disclosure will cause wrongful loss or gain
preventive_measures: Include strong data protection clauses in all contracts
Provide employee training on data privacy
Enforce strict access controls to personal data
Implement Data Leak Prevention (DLP) systems
Conduct regular privacy audits
Perform thorough due diligence on vendors
evidence_required: Contract showing confidentiality and data protection obligations
Proof of disclosure (e.g., email, data log)
Details of the personal information involved
Evidence suggesting knowledge of potential loss/gain

laws_master.full_description: Whoever knowingly creates, publishes or otherwise makes available a Digital Signature Certificate for any fraudulent or unlawful purpose. [citation:4]
legal_ingredients: Knowingly created, published, or made available
For a fraudulent or unlawful purpose
preventive_measures: Verify identity thoroughly before issuing a DSC
Maintain detailed logs of all certificates issued
Establish a clear certificate revocation procedure
Conduct regular audits of issued certificates
Report any suspicious or fraudulent certificates to authorities
Ensure secure storage of private keys by subscribers
evidence_required: Issuance records from the Certifying Authority
Evidence demonstrating the fraudulent or unlawful purpose
Communication showing the intent to defraud

laws_master.act_name: IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021
laws_master.full_description: Intermediaries (social media platforms, apps, etc.) must exercise due diligence. They must inform users not to host unlawful content including obscene material, defamation, hate speech, deepfakes, and content that invades privacy. [citation:1]
legal_ingredients: Lack of proper user agreement and notice

punishment.details: Loss of safe harbour protection under Section 79 of IT Act. Can be liable for content.

preventive_measures: Publish clear terms of service and user agreements
Appoint a Grievance Officer (name and contact details)
Remove unlawful content within 36 hours of complaint (24 hours for privacy/impersonation)
Implement automated tools to detect and remove prohibited content
Inform users about rules and consequences of violation
Comply with government advisories on deepfakes and misinformation
evidence_required: Terms of service and privacy policy documents
Action taken reports on user complaints

laws_master.full_description: Whoever intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without consent, moves that property. In the cyber context, digital data is considered movable property if it can be transferred, copied, or moved. [citation:4]
legal_ingredients: Taking movable property (including digital data) out of possession
Movement of the property (e.g., copying/transferring data)
preventive_measures: Implement data encryption at rest and in transit
Enforce strict access controls
Maintain regular backups in secure locations
Deploy Data Loss Prevention (DLP) software
Establish clear employee exit protocols to revoke access
Monitor and audit all large data transfers
evidence_required: Access logs showing unauthorized access or data movement
Data transfer records with timestamps and volume

laws_master.full_description: Whoever dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use any movable property (including digital data) shall be punished. [citation:4]
legal_ingredients: Conversion of property for own use
preventive_measures: Establish clear data ownership and usage policies
Implement role-based access restrictions
Classify data based on sensitivity
Provide employee training on proper data handling
Maintain a detailed asset inventory
Conduct regular audits of data access and usage
evidence_required: Access logs showing the accused accessed the data

laws_master.full_description: Whoever by deceiving any person fraudulently or dishonestly induces that person to deliver any property, or to consent that any person shall retain any property, or intentionally induces the person to do or omit anything which causes damage or harm. [citation:4]
legal_ingredients: Delivery of property or consent to retain property
Act or omission causing damage or harm
preventive_measures: Verify online offers and deals from independent sources
Check website authenticity and look for secure payment gateways
Never make advance payments to unknown individuals
Read terms and conditions carefully
Be vigilant against phishing emails and messages
Do not click on suspicious links
evidence_required: Website URLs involved in the fraud
Any agreement or document provided by the deceiver

laws_master.full_description: Cheating by pretending to be another person, knowingly substituting one person for another, or representing that any person is a person other than such person is. [citation:4]
legal_ingredients: Knowingly substituting one person for another
preventive_measures: Enable two-factor authentication on all accounts
Never share OTPs, passwords, or banking details
Verify the caller's identity independently through official channels
Be extremely cautious of urgent or threatening requests
Use only official contact numbers from verified websites
Report suspicious calls and messages immediately
evidence_required: Phone numbers used by the impersonator
Email addresses used in the fraud

laws_master.full_description: Whoever with intent to cause or knowing likely to cause wrongful loss or damage to the public or any person, causes the destruction of any property, or any such change in any property or the situation thereof, diminishing its value or utility. [citation:4]
legal_ingredients: Intent to cause wrongful loss or damage
Diminishes the value or utility of property
Applicable to digital networks, servers, and online services
preventive_measures: Subscribe to DDoS protection services
Implement continuous network and system monitoring
Build redundant infrastructure to ensure service availability
Create and rehearse a comprehensive incident response plan
Conduct regular security testing, including stress tests
Implement traffic filtering and rate limiting
evidence_required: Network logs showing traffic patterns and anomalies
Records of service downtime and impact assessment

laws_master.full_description: Mandates lawful processing of personal data based on consent or legitimate uses. Requires clear notice, security safeguards, and breach reporting. Gives individuals rights to access, correction, and erasure. [citation:3][citation:6]
legal_ingredients: Consent requirement or legitimate use ground
Failure to implement reasonable security safeguards
Failure to notify breach to Board and affected individuals

punishment.details: Penalties up to ₹250 crore depending on severity and type of violation.

preventive_measures: Implement data encryption (at rest and in transit)
Appoint a Data Protection Officer (DPO) if required
Maintain a clear and published data breach response policy
Obtain clear, affirmative consent for data processing
Provide easy mechanisms for users to withdraw consent
Conduct regular Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIA) for high-risk processing
evidence_required: Consent records with timestamps and user acknowledgment
Data breach notification report to Data Protection Board
Records of data principal requests and responses

laws_master.full_description: Data Fiduciary must implement appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect personal data in its possession from breach, unauthorized access, disclosure or damage. [citation:3]
legal_ingredients: Personal data in possession of Data Fiduciary
Duty to protect data with reasonable safeguards
Failure leads to personal data breach

punishment.details: Penalties up to ₹250 crore for breach due to failure to maintain safeguards.

preventive_measures: Encrypt personal data at rest and in transit
Implement role-based access controls and strong authentication
Conduct regular security audits and vulnerability assessments
Perform penetration testing periodically
Maintain a tested security incident response plan
Ensure regular data backup and secure recovery procedures
Provide comprehensive employee security training

laws_master.full_description: Data Fiduciary must notify affected Data Principals and the Data Protection Board of a personal data breach without delay. A detailed report must follow within 72 hours. [citation:3][citation:6]
legal_ingredients: Notification to affected Data Principals is required
Notification to Data Protection Board is required
Notification must be timely (immediate, with 72-hour follow-up)

punishment.details: Penalties up to ₹200 crore for failure to notify the Board or affected individuals of a breach.

preventive_measures: Implement automated breach detection systems
Maintain a dedicated incident response team
Create pre-approved breach notification templates
Establish clear internal and external communication protocols
Maintain forensic investigation capability
Conduct regular tabletop exercises for breach scenarios
Keep an updated list of stakeholder contacts (Board, affected users)
evidence_required: Timestamp and method of breach detection
Initial notification sent to the Board
Details of affected data and individuals

laws_master.full_description: Additional obligations for notified Significant Data Fiduciaries (entities processing large volumes of sensitive data or posing significant risk) including appointment of a DPO, independent data auditor, and conducting Data Protection Impact Assessments. [citation:3][citation:6]
legal_ingredients: Notified as a Significant Data Fiduciary
Failure to appoint an independent data auditor
Failure to conduct Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA)
Failure to conduct periodic compliance audits

punishment.details: Enhanced penalties for non-compliance, as determined by the Data Protection Board.

preventive_measures: Appoint a qualified Data Protection Officer (DPO) based in India
Engage an independent data auditor for annual audits
Conduct DPIAs for all high-risk processing activities
Maintain comprehensive compliance documentation
Establish board-level privacy oversight
Implement algorithmic due diligence to ensure fairness
Prepare for potential data localization requirements
evidence_required: DPO appointment letter and contact details
Independent auditor engagement and audit reports
Compliance audit records and remediation plans

laws_master.full_description: Mandatory reporting of cybersecurity incidents including data breaches, intrusions, malware attacks, denial of service, and ransomware to CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing. [citation:4]
legal_ingredients: Incident falls within categories mandatorily reportable
Failure to report within 6 hours of noticing
preventive_measures: Establish 24x7 incident monitoring capability (SOC)
Develop an incident classification matrix to identify reportable events
Prepare pre-drafted reporting templates for quick use
Designate and train a reporting coordinator
Conduct regular incident response drills
Integrate all systems with a centralized SIEM for real-time alerting
evidence_required: Timestamp and method of incident detection
Copy of initial CERT-In notification (sent within 6 hours)
All updated and final incident investigation reports
Documentation of containment, eradication, and recovery actions

laws_master.full_description: All intermediaries, data centers, VPS providers, and cloud providers must retain all ICT system logs for 180 days within India for investigation purposes. [citation:4]
legal_ingredients: Entity is an intermediary/data center/VPS/cloud provider
Logs must be retained for 180 days
Logs must be stored within India
preventive_measures: Implement centralized log collection
Use immutable or Write-Once-Read-Many (WORM) storage for logs
Conduct regular log integrity checks (checksum/hash verification)
Implement automated log rotation and archival
Maintain secure, encrypted backups of all logs
Enforce strict access controls to log repositories
Document and maintain the log retention policy
evidence_required: Proof of log storage location (Indian data center)
Access control lists and access logs for the log repository

laws_master.full_description: All ICT systems must synchronize their clocks with trusted time sources (NIC/NPL) to ensure accurate timestamps for investigation and forensics. [citation:4]
preventive_measures: Establish a central NTP server hierarchy within the organization
Create and enforce configuration baselines for all ICT assets
Implement automated drift monitoring and alerting
Configure alerts for NTP synchronization failure
Conduct regular audits of system time settings
Document all trusted NTP sources used
evidence_required: NTP configuration records from servers, network devices, endpoints
Time synchronization logs showing drift and sync status
